citations.text: The study was approved by an independent ethics committee at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital in Gothenburg, Sweden (8883-12, 20121212) and registered at the Swedish National Database of Research and Development (identifier 113021; November 4, 2012; http://www.researchweb.org/is/vgr/project/113021).

The study was approved by an independent ethics committee at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital in Gothenburg, Sweden (8883-12, 20121212) and registered at the Swedish National Database of Research and Development (identifier 113021; November 4, 2012; http://www.researchweb.org/is/vgr/project/113021).
This is a clinical, prospective, controlled trial with two parallel groups, carried out at the NU county hospital group between March 2013 and July 2015.

other_measurements.label: ADL classified into three strata (independence, IADL-dependence, PADL-dependence)
named: In a complementary analysis, the functional abilities of patients were classified into independence, IADL-dependence, and PADL-dependence.

When ADLs were classified into three strata (independence, instrumental ADL-dependence, and personal ADL-dependence), changes to a more dependence-associated stratum were less prevalent in the intervention group (OR 0.194; 95% CI 0.085–0.444; P=0.0001).
result: When ADLs were classified in three strata (independence, IADL-dependence, and PADL-dependence), changes to a more dependence-associated stratum were less prevalent in the intervention group [11 (6.3%); n=176] than in the control group [33 (20.2%); n=163; P=0.0001].

other_measurements.label: ADL at index hospitalization (before discharge), ADL Staircase
named: ADL independence/dependence was assessed by using the ADL Staircase before discharge.31

other_measurements.label: Katz Index for loss of basal ADL at 3 months (sample size basis)
named: The sample size calculation was based on change in functional capacity measured as the loss of basal ADL according to the Katz Index after 3 months (significance level 0.05, power 80%).
second_look: At the 3-month follow-up, decline in ADLs according to the ADL Staircase was less prevalent in the intervention group [24 (14.1%); n=170] than in the control group 98 (63.6%); n=154; P<0.0001, [Table 2].

For the control group, the average change was 1.1 step (SD 1.6) down the ADL Staircase. For the intervention group, the average change was 0.2 step (SD 1.1) up, that is, the majority presented with no change in ADL.

In multiple logistic regression analyses, treatment in a CGA unit was independently associated with lower risk of a decline in ADLs (odds ratio [OR] 0.093; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.052–0.16; Table 3).

other_analyses.label: Cox regression model for primary and secondary outcomes
named: Associations of the intervention with the primary and secondary outcomes were assessed by either Cox regression or a multiple logistic regression model adjusted for relevant prognostic variables (sex, age, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index score).
